note: Terms and definitions are quoted verbatim from the upstream glossary; aliases, closeTerms, local and antiPatterns are this repository's. The motion-vocabulary/* records in component-source-catalog.json are generated from this file by scripts/refresh-motion-vocabulary.cjs --catalog.

categories.name: Movement & Transforms
categories.description: changing an element's position, size, or angle

categories.name: Transitions Between States
categories.description: connecting one state, view, or element to another

categories.name: Scroll
categories.description: motion tied to scrolling or navigating between views

categories.name: Easing
categories.description: how speed changes over an animation

categories.name: Spring Animations
categories.description: physics-based motion as an alternative to fixed-duration easing

categories.name: Looping & Ambient Motion
categories.description: animations that run on their own

categories.name: Polish & Effects
categories.description: the small touches that separate good from great

categories.name: Performance
categories.description: what keeps motion smooth instead of stuttering

categories.name: Principles to Know
categories.description: concepts that guide when and how to animate

terms.definition: Element appears or disappears by changing opacity.

en: gradually appears from transparent
fades away until it is invisible
opacity going from 0 to 1

closeTerms.difference: A crossfade is two elements trading places in one spot; a fade is one element changing opacity.
A reveal uncovers content along an edge with a clip or mask; a fade changes the opacity of the whole element at once.

terms.definition: Element enters by sliding in from off-screen (left, right, top, or bottom).

en: comes in from the side of the screen
panel moves in from off-screen
drawer sliding in from the edge

closeTerms.difference: A direction-aware transition picks the slide direction from forward or back navigation; a slide in has one fixed direction.
A scroll reveal is triggered by the element entering the viewport; a slide in is triggered by the element being added.

terms.definition: Element grows from smaller to full size as it appears, often paired with a fade.

en: grows from a bit smaller to full size while appearing
zooms up slightly as it shows
zh: 从小一点放大到正常大小出现

closeTerms.difference: Pop in overshoots past full size and settles back; scale in stops exactly at full size.
Scale in says how the element appears; origin-aware says where it grows from.
Scale is the transform itself; scale in is an entrance that uses it.

terms.definition: Element appears with a slight overshoot, like it bounces into place.

en: appears with a little overshoot and then settles
the bouncy thing when a popover opens
pops onto the screen slightly too big then comes back
zh: 弹出来的时候稍微过头再回正
先放大过头一点再缩回来

closeTerms.difference: Bounce is the spring behaviour, overshoot and settle, on any motion; pop in is specifically an entrance that uses it.
Scale in has no overshoot; it stops exactly at full size.

terms.definition: Content is uncovered gradually, often by animating a clip-path or mask.

en: content gets uncovered gradually like a curtain pulling back
wipes into view
unmasked bit by bit
zh: 像拉开幕布一样慢慢露出来

closeTerms.difference: Clip-path is a tool with hard edges; reveal is the effect, whichever tool draws it.
Mask is a tool with soft, fadeable edges; reveal is the effect.
A scroll reveal is triggered by entering the viewport and may only fade or slide; a reveal uncovers along an edge.

terms.definition: The animation an element plays when it's added to or removed from the screen.

en: the animation when something is added to or removed from the page
mount and unmount animation
how it comes in and how it leaves
zh: 元素出现和消失时播的动画

closeTerms.difference: A page transition covers a whole route change; enter and exit belong to one element.
Fade is one way to enter or exit; enter and exit name the moment, not the look.

terms.definition: Defined points in an animation (0%, 50%, 100%) that the browser fills the gaps between.

en: the defined points at 0%, 50% and 100% of an animation
waypoints the browser fills in between
zh: 在 0%、50%、100% 定好的几个状态点

closeTerms.difference: Keyframes are the fixed points; interpolation is the filling between them.
A stepped animation jumps between points; keyframes are normally interpolated smoothly.

terms.definition: Generating all the in-between frames between a start and end value, so motion is continuous.

en: generating the in-between frames from start to end
smoothly filling the gap between two values
tweening
zh: 自动算出起点和终点之间的中间帧

closeTerms.difference: Keyframes are the fixed points you define; interpolation generates what lies between them.
Easing shapes the rate of the interpolation; it is not the interpolation itself.

terms.definition: Animate several items one after another with a small delay between each, creating a cascade.

en: items come in one after another
list items appear one by one with a small delay
a cascade where each element is slightly later than the last
zh: 一个接一个地依次出现

closeTerms.difference: Stagger is one repeated delay across similar items; orchestration times different animations into one whole.
A delay is one wait; a stagger is a delay that grows item by item.

terms.definition: Deliberately timing multiple animations so they feel like one coordinated motion.

en: timing several animations so they read as one move
choreographing multiple elements together
zh: 把多个动画安排得像一个整体动作

closeTerms.difference: Stagger is one tool of orchestration: the same delay repeated across similar items.

terms.definition: Time before an animation starts.

en: wait before the animation starts
pause before it begins moving
zh: 动画开始前先等一会儿

closeTerms.difference: A stagger is a delay that grows item by item across a group.
Duration is how long the animation runs; delay is the wait before it runs.

terms.definition: How long an animation takes.

en: how long the animation takes
length of the animation in milliseconds

closeTerms.difference: Perceptual duration is the spring counterpart: how long it feels finished, since a spring has no fixed end.
Delay is the wait before the animation; duration is the animation itself.

terms.definition: Whether an element keeps its first or last frame's styles before the animation starts or after it ends (e.g. forwards).

en: keeps the last frame's styles after the animation ends
stays at the end state instead of snapping back
animation-fill-mode forwards
zh: 动画播完后停在最后一帧不跳回去
动画开始前先套用第一帧的样式

closeTerms.difference: Fill mode decides what the element looks like during the delay and after the end; delay only sets the wait.

terms.definition: An animation that is divided into discrete steps, like a countdown timer.

en: moves in discrete jumps instead of smoothly
ticks like a countdown timer
frame-by-frame sprite steps
zh: 一格一格跳着走而不是平滑过渡
像倒计时那样一下一下跳

closeTerms.difference: Linear is constant speed but still continuous; stepped has no in-between frames.
A number ticker rolls digits to a value; a stepped animation is any motion cut into jumps.

terms.definition: Move an element along the X or Y axis.

en: move an element along x or y
shift it sideways or up and down
zh: 沿 X 或 Y 轴移动

closeTerms.difference: Slide in is an entrance built on translate.
Drag is translation driven by the pointer.

terms.definition: Make an element bigger or smaller.

en: make it bigger or smaller
resize it with a transform

closeTerms.difference: Scale in is an entrance that uses scale.
Press feedback is a small scale-down tied to a click or tap.
Pulse is a scale or opacity change that repeats.

terms.definition: Spin an element around a point.

en: spin an element around a point
turn it by some degrees

closeTerms.difference: 3D tilt or flip rotates around the X or Y axis for depth; rotate spins flat in the plane.
Orbit moves an element around another one; rotate spins it in place.

terms.definition: Slant an element along the X or Y axis, shearing it out of its rectangular shape.

en: slant the element so it looks sheared
tilts into a parallelogram
zh: 把矩形拉歪成平行四边形

closeTerms.difference: Rotate keeps the rectangle; skew shears it.
A 3D tilt keeps right angles in its own plane and adds depth; skew distorts the shape in 2D.

terms.definition: Rotate in 3D space (rotateX / rotateY) to add depth.

en: card flips over in 3D
tilts toward the cursor with depth
rotateX rotateY card flip

closeTerms.difference: Rotate spins flat in the plane; tilt and flip turn around the X or Y axis.
Perspective sets how strong the depth of a tilt or flip looks.

terms.definition: How strong the 3D effect looks — a lower value exaggerates depth, like the viewer is closer.

en: how strong the 3D depth looks
the viewer distance for a 3D transform
zh: 观察距离越近透视越夸张

closeTerms.difference: Tilt and flip are the rotations; perspective is how deep they look.
Parallax fakes depth with layers moving at different speeds; perspective is real 3D projection.

terms.definition: The anchor point a scale or rotation grows or spins from.

en: the anchor point it scales or rotates from
pivot point of the transform

closeTerms.difference: Transform origin is the CSS anchor; an origin-aware animation sets that anchor to the trigger.

terms.definition: An element animates out of its trigger, like a popover growing from the button that opened it instead of from its own center which is the default in CSS.

en: popover grows out of the button that opened it
menu expands from its trigger instead of from its center
dropdown scales from where you clicked
zh: 弹出层从触发它的按钮里长出来
菜单从点击的位置展开而不是从中心

closeTerms.difference: Transform origin is the property; origin-aware is the decision to point it at the trigger.
Scale in says how the surface appears; origin-aware says where it grows from.
In a shared element transition the trigger itself travels and becomes the new surface; origin-aware only anchors the new surface to the trigger.

terms.definition: One element fades out as another fades in, in the same spot.

en: one thing fades out while another fades in at the same place
two images dissolve into each other
zh: 一个淡出的同时另一个在原地淡入

closeTerms.difference: A morph changes the shape itself; a crossfade only blends opacity.
A fade is one element; a crossfade is two swapping in one spot.
A view transition defaults to a crossfade but can also connect shared elements.

terms.definition: A change that keeps the user oriented by visually connecting before and after. For example, making the same rectangle bigger and smaller.

en: the change keeps you oriented by connecting before and after
the same box just gets bigger instead of being replaced
zh: 变化前后在视觉上连得起来不让人迷失
同一个矩形变大变小而不是换一个

closeTerms.difference: A shared element transition is one technique for continuity: an element travels between two places.
Spatial consistency is the principle; a continuity transition is a change that follows it.
A layout animation is continuity for one element whose box changed.

terms.definition: One shape smoothly turns into another shape, e.g. Dynamic Island.

en: one shape smoothly turns into another shape
icon transforms into a different icon
one image turns into another image
the Dynamic Island changing shape
zh: 一个形状平滑地变成另一个形状

closeTerms.difference: Crossfade if the two simply fade over each other in the same spot and nothing changes shape.
Shared element transition if an element travels and transforms from one position into another.
Text morph is the same idea applied to characters when a label changes.

terms.definition: An element travels and transforms from one position into another, like a thumbnail expanding into a card.

en: thumbnail expands into the full card
an element flies from the list into the detail page
shared layout animation
hero image travels to its place on the next screen
zh: 缩略图放大成详情卡片
同一个元素从列表飞到详情页

closeTerms.difference: A layout animation is one element reacting to its own change of size or position; a shared element transition links two elements in different places or views. Motion's "shared layout animation" (layoutId) is this term, not layout animation.
A morph changes shape in place; a shared element also travels.
A view transition is a browser mechanism that can carry a shared element.
Continuity transition is the broader idea; a shared element is one way to get it.

terms.definition: When an element's size or position changes, it animates to the new spot instead of snapping.

en: items glide to their new position instead of jumping when the layout changes
the box animates to its new size
siblings smoothly shift when one is removed
zh: 布局变化时元素滑到新位置而不是瞬间跳过去
尺寸变了以后平滑过渡到新大小

closeTerms.difference: A layout animation animates one element whose own size or position changed. A "shared layout animation" (Motion's layoutId) connects two different elements and is a shared element transition.
Accordion or collapse is the height-only case with content shown or hidden.
Layout thrashing is the cost when the effect is built by animating layout properties every frame.
Drag to reorder uses a layout animation for the items that make room.

terms.definition: A section smoothly expands and collapses its height to show or hide content.

en: section expands and collapses its height
FAQ row opens to show the answer
disclosure panel smoothly unfolding
zh: 点一下内容区域高度展开再点收起

closeTerms.difference: A layout animation covers any size or position change; an accordion is the height of a section opening and closing.
A reveal uncovers content without moving what is below it; an accordion pushes the following content.

terms.definition: Content slides one way going forward and the opposite way going back, so navigation has a sense of direction.

en: slides one way going forward and the other way going back
next page comes from the right and going back comes from the left
tabs slide according to which way you moved
zh: 前进往一边滑后退往反方向滑
根据切换方向决定从左还是从右进来

closeTerms.difference: A slide in has one fixed direction; this one chooses the direction from the navigation.
A page transition is any animation between routes; direction-aware is one way to design it.

terms.definition: Elements fade or slide into place as they enter the viewport.

en: elements fade or slide into place as you scroll down to them
sections appear when they enter the viewport
zh: 滚动到的时候内容淡入或滑进来

closeTerms.difference: A scroll reveal fires once at a threshold and plays on its own clock; a scroll-driven animation is scrubbed by the scroll position.
A reveal uncovers along an edge whatever triggers it; a scroll reveal is defined by its viewport trigger.

terms.definition: An animation whose progress is tied directly to scroll position.

en: animation progress follows the scroll position
scrubs forward and backward as you scroll
scroll-linked progress bar
zh: 动画进度跟着滚动条走
往回滚动画也跟着倒放

closeTerms.difference: A scroll reveal only starts on scroll and then plays by itself; a scroll-driven animation stops when the scroll stops.
Parallax is one scroll-driven effect: layers moving at different speeds.

terms.definition: Background and foreground move at different speeds while scrolling, creating depth.

en: background moves slower than the foreground while scrolling
layers drift at different speeds to feel deep
zh: 滚动时背景比前景动得慢
前后层以不同速度移动产生纵深

closeTerms.difference: Scroll-driven animation is the general mechanism; parallax is the depth effect built on it.
Perspective is real 3D projection; parallax fakes depth with speed differences.

terms.definition: An animation that plays when navigating from one page or route to another.

en: animation between one page and the next
route change animation
zh: 从一个路由跳到另一个时的转场

closeTerms.difference: A view transition is the browser feature that can produce a page transition.
Direction-aware is a page transition whose direction follows forward and back.
A shared element transition carries one element across the page change.

terms.definition: The browser morphs between two states or pages, connecting shared elements.

en: the browser morphs between two page states
View Transitions API snapshot crossfade
old and new states get connected automatically
zh: 浏览器自动在两个状态之间做变形衔接
用 View Transitions API 做的状态衔接

closeTerms.difference: A page transition is the effect between routes, however it is built; a view transition is the browser doing it.
A view transition connects shared elements when they are named; the shared element transition is that connection.
With nothing named, a view transition is a crossfade of the two states.

terms.definition: Visual change when the cursor moves over an element.

en: changes when the mouse is over it
card lifts when you point at it

closeTerms.difference: Hover answers the pointer being over the element; press feedback answers the click or tap itself.

terms.definition: A subtle scale-down when an element is clicked, so it feels physical.

en: button shrinks slightly when you press it
subtle scale-down on click so it feels physical
squishes a bit on tap
zh: 按钮按下去的时候缩小一点

closeTerms.difference: A ripple spreads from the touch point; press feedback scales the whole element.
A hover effect answers the pointer resting over the element, before any press.
Squash and stretch deforms the shape unevenly; press feedback is a small uniform scale.

terms.definition: A progress effect that fills up while the user holds a button.

en: keep the button held and a bar fills until it confirms
press and hold to delete
zh: 按住按钮进度条慢慢填满才生效

closeTerms.difference: Press feedback answers a single press at once; hold to confirm needs the press to last.

terms.definition: Moving an element by grabbing it, often with momentum when released.

en: grab an element and move it around
pick it up with the pointer and it keeps gliding when released
zh: 松手后还带着惯性滑一段

closeTerms.difference: Drag to reorder is a drag inside a list where the other items make room.
Swipe to dismiss is a drag whose release closes the element.
Momentum is what the element does after the drag is released.

terms.definition: Dragging items in a list to rearrange them, while the others shift to make room.

en: drag list items to rearrange them while the others move out of the way
sortable list
zh: 拖动列表项重新排列其他项自动让位

closeTerms.difference: Drag is the free gesture; reorder adds a list whose items shift.
The items that make room move with a layout animation.

terms.definition: Dragging an element off-screen to close it, like a drawer or toast.

en: flick a toast off the screen to close it
drag the drawer down to dismiss it
swipe a card away
zh: 把通知往旁边一划就关掉
向下拖动抽屉把它收起

closeTerms.difference: Drag moves an element and leaves it there; swipe to dismiss closes it past a distance or speed.
Rubber-banding resists in the direction that does not dismiss.

terms.definition: Resistance and snap-back when you drag past a boundary (the iOS overscroll feel).

en: resists and snaps back when you pull too far
the iOS overscroll stretch
elastic resistance past the edge of a list
zh: 拉过头有阻力松手弹回去
iOS 滚动到头还能拉一点再回弹

closeTerms.difference: Bounce is a spring overshooting its target on the way in; rubber-banding is resistance while you drag beyond a limit.
Momentum carries motion after release; rubber-banding pushes back during the drag.
Swipe to dismiss lets the element go; rubber-banding brings it back.

terms.definition: A quick side-to-side jitter signaling an error or rejected input.

en: jitters side to side when the password is wrong
quick horizontal shake for an error
the input shakes its head at you
zh: 输错密码时输入框左右晃几下

closeTerms.difference: Pulse is a gentle repeating change that invites attention; a shake is one sharp rejection.
Bounce settles after reaching a target; a shake returns to where it started.

terms.definition: A circle expanding from the point of a tap, confirming the press.

en: a circle spreads out from where you tapped
Material-style ink ripple on click
zh: 从点击的位置扩散出一个圆

closeTerms.difference: Press feedback scales the whole element; a ripple starts at the touch point.
Pulse repeats by itself; a ripple is one answer to one tap.

terms.definition: The rate at which an animation speeds up or slows down.

en: how the speed changes during the animation
the acceleration curve of a motion
zh: 动画过程中速度的变化方式

closeTerms.difference: Cubic-bezier is one way to define an easing.
A spring gets its speed changes from physics and has no fixed duration.
Interpolation produces the in-between values; easing decides how fast it moves through them.

terms.definition: Starts fast, ends slow. The default for most UI and anything responding to the user.

en: starts fast and slows down at the end
decelerates into place

closeTerms.difference: Ease-in is the reverse: slow start, fast end.
Ease-in-out is slow at both ends.

terms.definition: Starts slow, ends fast. Usually avoided; can feel sluggish.

en: starts slow and speeds up
accelerates away

closeTerms.difference: Ease-out is the reverse: fast start, slow end.
Ease-in-out also slows down again at the end.

terms.definition: Slow, fast, slow. Good for elements already on screen moving from A to B.

en: slow then fast then slow
accelerates then decelerates between two points

closeTerms.difference: Ease-out has no slow start, so it answers input sooner.
Ease-in-out is the same at both ends; an asymmetric easing is not.

terms.definition: Constant speed. Avoid for UI; reserve for spinners or marquees.

en: moves at constant speed with no acceleration
robotic even pace

closeTerms.difference: Easing is any change of speed; linear is the case with none.
Stepped jumps between values; linear moves through them at an even rate.

terms.definition: A custom easing curve you define for precise control.

en: a custom easing curve with four numbers
hand-tuned bezier timing function
zh: 用四个数值自定义的缓动曲线

closeTerms.difference: Easing is the concept; cubic-bezier is one notation for it.
A spring is described by physics values and has no fixed duration; a cubic-bezier runs over a set duration.

terms.definition: A curve that accelerates and decelerates at different rates. Feels more alive than a symmetric one.

en: speeds up and slows down at different rates
curve that is quick to start but takes long to settle
zh: 加速和减速的快慢不一样
起步快收尾拖得长的曲线

closeTerms.difference: Ease-in-out mirrors its start and end; an asymmetric easing does not.
A cubic-bezier is how an asymmetric easing is usually written.

terms.definition: Motion driven by physics (tension, mass, damping) rather than a set duration.

en: motion driven by physics instead of a fixed duration
springy natural movement
feels like it is attached to a spring
zh: 由物理参数驱动而不是固定时长
像被弹簧拉着一样自然

closeTerms.difference: Easing is a curve over a fixed duration; a spring has no fixed duration.
Bounce is the optional overshoot of a spring; a spring can also settle with none.

terms.definition: How strongly the spring pulls toward its target. Higher feels snappier.

en: how hard the spring pulls toward the target
a higher value makes it snappier
zh: 弹簧往目标拉的力度越大越干脆

closeTerms.difference: Damping decides how fast the spring settles; stiffness decides how hard it pulls.
Mass is the weight being pulled.

terms.definition: How quickly a spring settles. Lower damping means more bounce and oscillation.

en: how quickly the spring stops wobbling
less of it means more oscillation

closeTerms.difference: Stiffness is the pull toward the target; damping is the brake.
Bounce is what low damping looks like.

terms.definition: How heavy the animated element feels. More mass makes it slower and more sluggish.

en: how heavy the element feels
a heavier object moves slower and more sluggishly

closeTerms.difference: Stiffness is the force; mass is what the force has to move.
Damping removes energy; mass stores it.

terms.definition: A spring that overshoots and settles, adding playfulness.

en: overshoots the target and settles back
playful springy overshoot
wobbles a little before coming to rest

closeTerms.difference: Pop in is an entrance with a slight overshoot; bounce is the spring behaviour and applies to any motion.
Damping is the value that controls how much bounce there is.
Rubber-banding is resistance while dragging past a limit, not overshoot on arrival.

terms.definition: How long a spring feels finished, even though it keeps micro-settling underneath.

en: how long a spring feels finished even though it is still settling
the visible length of a spring animation
zh: 弹簧看起来已经停了其实还在微调的那个时间

closeTerms.difference: Duration is exact and belongs to eased animations; perceptual duration is the felt length of a spring.

terms.definition: Motion that carries velocity, especially after a drag or interruption.

en: keeps moving after you let go
carries its speed after a flick
inertia scrolling
zh: 松手后带着速度继续滑

closeTerms.difference: Velocity is the measured speed and direction; momentum is the motion that keeps carrying it.
Drag is the part under the pointer; momentum is the part after release.
Rubber-banding resists at a boundary; momentum continues freely.

terms.definition: How fast and in which direction an element is moving. A spring carries it into the next animation when interrupted, so a flicked element keeps its speed.

en: how fast and in which direction it is moving
the speed handed over when an animation is interrupted
zh: 元素移动的快慢和方向
被打断时带进下一个动画的速度

closeTerms.difference: Momentum is motion that continues because of velocity.
An interruptible animation keeps the current velocity when it is redirected.

terms.definition: An animation that can be smoothly redirected mid-flight instead of finishing first.

en: can be redirected halfway instead of finishing first
click again mid-animation and it reverses smoothly
does not lock out input while animating
zh: 动到一半可以平滑改方向不用等播完
动画中途再点一次能顺滑反向

closeTerms.difference: Velocity is what an interruptible animation carries into the new direction.
Springs are the usual way to get one, because they continue from the current value and velocity.

terms.definition: Text or content that scrolls continuously in a loop.

en: text scrolls sideways forever
logo strip that keeps sliding in a loop
news-ticker style scrolling
zh: 文字一直横向滚动循环

closeTerms.difference: Loop is any repeating animation; a marquee is content travelling in one direction on repeat.
A marquee moves by itself; a scroll-driven animation moves only when the user scrolls.

terms.definition: An animation that repeats, a set number of times or infinitely.

en: the animation repeats over and over
plays infinitely

closeTerms.difference: A plain loop jumps back to the start; alternate plays backward to get there.
An idle animation is a loop with a role: showing that a resting element is alive.

terms.definition: A loop that plays forward then reverses each iteration, instead of jumping back to the start.

en: plays forward then backward each time
goes there and back instead of jumping to the start
ping-pong loop
zh: 来回摆动而不是跳回起点

closeTerms.difference: A loop restarts from the beginning each time; alternate reverses.
Pulse is usually an alternate loop of scale or opacity.

terms.definition: An element circling around another in a continuous path.

en: one element circles around another
dots revolving around a center
zh: 一个元素绕着另一个转圈

closeTerms.difference: Rotate spins an element in place; orbit moves it around something else.

terms.definition: A gentle repeating scale or opacity change to draw attention.

en: gently grows and shrinks repeatedly to get attention
soft repeating glow on a notification dot
heartbeat-like throb
zh: 轻轻地反复放大缩小吸引注意

closeTerms.difference: Float changes position; pulse changes scale or opacity.
A shake is one sharp rejection; a pulse is a gentle repeat.
A ripple answers one tap; a pulse repeats unprompted.

terms.definition: A gentle, continuous up-and-down drift that makes a static element feel alive and weightless.

en: drifts gently up and down
hovers in place like it is weightless
bobbing illustration
zh: 像没有重量一样悬着飘

closeTerms.difference: Pulse changes scale or opacity in place; float changes position.
Float is one kind of idle animation.

terms.definition: Subtle motion that plays while an element is just sitting there, waiting to be interacted with.

en: subtle motion while nothing is happening
moves a little while waiting to be clicked
ambient motion on a resting element
zh: 没人操作时自己轻微地动

closeTerms.difference: Loop is the mechanism; idle animation is the role.
Float is one idle animation: a slow vertical drift.
A pulse asks for attention; an idle animation only shows the element is alive.

terms.definition: A blur filter used to soften an element or mask tiny imperfections.

en: soften the element with a blur filter
goes out of focus during the transition
zh: 用模糊滤镜把元素变柔
过渡时糊一下掩盖瑕疵

closeTerms.difference: A mask hides parts of an element; blur softens all of it.
A fade changes opacity; blur changes sharpness. They are often used together.

terms.definition: Clipping an element to a shape, used for reveals, masks, and before/after sliders.

en: cut the element to a shape with hard edges
crop it to a circle or an inset rectangle and animate the crop

closeTerms.difference: Clip-path cuts along a geometric shape with a hard edge; mask hides with an image or gradient, so its edge can be soft and fade.
Reveal is the effect; clip-path is one way to draw it.
A before/after slider is a clip-path whose edge follows a draggable divider.

terms.definition: Hiding or revealing parts of an element using a shape or gradient — like clip-path, but with soft, fadeable edges.

en: hide parts of it with a soft gradient edge
content fades out toward the edge of a scroll area
feathered cutout
zh: 用渐变把一部分柔和地藏起来

closeTerms.difference: Mask hides with an image or gradient, so its edge can be soft and fade; clip-path cuts along a geometric shape with a hard edge.
Reveal is the effect; mask is one way to draw it.
Blur softens the whole element; a mask hides part of it.

terms.definition: A draggable divider that wipes between two overlaid images to compare them.

en: drag a divider to compare two images
comparison slider wiping between before and after
zh: 拖动中间的分割线对比两张图

closeTerms.difference: Clip-path is the technique underneath; the slider is the component.
Drag is the gesture that moves the divider.

terms.definition: An SVG path that draws itself in, like an invisible pen tracing it.

en: an SVG path draws itself
the outline traces itself like an invisible pen
a signature being written
zh: 像有支看不见的笔在描

closeTerms.difference: A reveal uncovers finished content; line drawing grows a stroke along its path.
Typewriter adds whole characters; line drawing traces a stroke.

terms.definition: Text that animates character by character when it changes, drawing attention to the new value.

en: text changes character by character into the new value
label letters shuffle into the next word
zh: 文本变化时逐字过渡到新内容
字符一个个变成新的词

closeTerms.difference: Morph is one shape becoming another; text morph applies it per character when text changes.
A number ticker rolls digits to a value; text morph handles any text.
Typewriter makes text appear; text morph replaces text that is already there.

terms.definition: A placeholder with a moving sheen shown while content loads.

en: grey placeholder with a sheen moving across while loading
loading skeleton blocks
zh: 加载时灰色占位块上有一道光扫过去

closeTerms.difference: A pulsing placeholder changes opacity as a whole; a shimmer moves a highlight across it.

terms.definition: Digits rolling or counting up to a value.

en: digits roll up to the value
counter counting up
odometer-style rolling numbers
zh: 数字一位位滚到目标值

closeTerms.difference: Tabular numbers are the type setting that keeps a ticker from shifting sideways.
Text morph handles any text; a ticker is for numbers and shows them counting.
A stepped animation is any motion in jumps; a ticker counts toward a value.

terms.definition: Fixed-width digits so numbers don't shift around as they change. Essential for tickers, timers, and counters.

en: fixed-width digits so numbers do not jiggle as they change
monospaced figures for timers
zh: 数字变化时宽度不变不会左右抖

closeTerms.difference: A number ticker is the animation; tabular numbers keep its digits in place.

terms.definition: Text appearing one character at a time, as if being typed.

en: text appears one character at a time as if typed
typing effect with a blinking caret
zh: 文字一个字一个字打出来

closeTerms.difference: Text morph replaces existing text; typewriter adds text that was not there.
A per-character stagger animates characters that are all laid out already; typewriter appends them.
Line drawing traces strokes; typewriter adds whole characters.

terms.definition: Frames drawn per second. 60fps is the baseline for smooth motion; 120fps on newer displays.

en: how many frames are drawn each second
60fps smoothness

closeTerms.difference: A dropped frame is one frame missing from the rate.
Jank is what an uneven frame rate looks like.

terms.definition: Visible stutter when the browser drops frames because it can't keep up with the animation.

en: the animation stutters visibly
choppy laggy motion when the browser cannot keep up

closeTerms.difference: A dropped frame is a single missed frame; jank is the stutter you see from them.
Layout thrashing is a common cause of jank.

terms.definition: A frame the browser missed its deadline to draw, causing a tiny hitch in motion.

en: a frame the browser failed to draw in time
tiny hitch in the motion
zh: 浏览器没赶上画的那一帧

closeTerms.difference: Jank is the visible result of dropped frames.
Frame rate is the count per second; a dropped frame lowers it for a moment.

terms.definition: Letting the GPU move or fade an element on its own layer without redoing layout or paint.

en: the GPU moves a layer without redoing layout or paint
transform and opacity run on the compositor
zh: 交给 GPU 在独立图层上移动不重新布局重绘

closeTerms.difference: Hardware acceleration is the principle; compositing is the browser step that delivers it.
will-change asks for the layer ahead of time; compositing is what the layer allows.
Layout thrashing is the opposite path: layout recalculated every frame.

terms.definition: A CSS hint that an element is about to animate, so the browser can promote it to its own layer ahead of time.

en: CSS hint that an element is about to animate
promote it to its own layer ahead of time
zh: 提前告诉浏览器这个元素要动

closeTerms.difference: Compositing is the work the GPU does on a layer; will-change only requests the layer early.
Hardware acceleration comes from which properties animate; will-change is an optional hint on top.

terms.definition: Animating properties like width, height, top, or left that force the browser to recalculate layout every frame, causing jank.

en: animating width, height, top or left forces layout every frame
reflow on every frame makes it janky
zh: 动画改宽高或 top left 导致每帧重新计算布局

closeTerms.difference: Jank is the symptom; layout thrashing is one cause.
A layout animation is the intended effect; thrashing is the expensive way to build it.
Compositing avoids layout; thrashing triggers it every frame.

terms.definition: Motion should serve a function — orient, give feedback, show relationships — not just decorate.

en: motion that has a job instead of decorating
animate only when it helps orient or gives feedback
zh: 动效要有功能而不是装饰

closeTerms.difference: Frequency of use decides how much of a purposeful animation survives repetition.
Feeling faster is one purpose an animation can serve.

terms.definition: A small wind-up in the opposite direction before a move, hinting at what's about to happen.

en: a small wind-up in the opposite direction before moving
pulls back before it launches
zh: 动之前先往反方向收一下

closeTerms.difference: Anticipation comes before the main move; follow-through comes after it.
Squash and stretch deforms the shape; anticipation moves it the other way first.

terms.definition: Parts of an element keep moving and settle slightly after the main motion stops, adding weight.

en: parts keep moving and settle after the main motion stops
trailing bits lag behind then catch up
zh: 主体停了附属部分还继续动一下再停

closeTerms.difference: Anticipation is the wind-up before; follow-through is the settle after.
Bounce is the whole element overshooting; follow-through is parts of it arriving late.

terms.definition: Deforming an element as it moves to convey weight, speed, and flexibility.

en: deforms as it moves to show weight and speed
flattens on impact and elongates when fast
jelly-like squish
zh: 运动时形变表现重量和速度

closeTerms.difference: Press feedback is a small uniform scale-down; squash and stretch changes width and height unevenly.
Bounce is overshoot in position or scale; squash and stretch is the shape deforming.

terms.definition: The right animation makes an interface feel faster, even when it isn't.

en: animation that makes the interface feel faster than it is
feels quick even though the wait is the same
zh: 实际没变快但体感更快

closeTerms.difference: Purposeful animation is the general rule; perceived performance is one purpose.
A skeleton with a shimmer is a common tool for it.

terms.definition: The more often a user sees an animation, the shorter and subtler it should be.

en: the more often it is seen the shorter and subtler it should be
animations used a hundred times a day should nearly disappear
zh: 越常见的动画越要短越要轻
一天看上百次的动效应该几乎没有

closeTerms.difference: Purpose decides whether to animate; frequency decides how much.
Duration is the value that frequency of use shortens.

terms.definition: Animating so an element keeps its identity and position across states, so users never lose track of where things went.

en: elements keep their identity and position across states
you never lose track of where something went
things come back from where they left
zh: 元素在状态之间保持位置和身份
不会让人找不到东西去哪了

closeTerms.difference: A continuity transition is a change that keeps spatial consistency.
A shared element transition is the strongest form: the element visibly travels.
Direction-aware transitions keep the direction of navigation consistent.

terms.definition: Animating transform and opacity lets the GPU keep motion smooth.

en: animate transform and opacity so the GPU keeps it smooth
GPU-accelerated animation
zh: 只动 transform 和 opacity 让 GPU 来跑

closeTerms.difference: Compositing is the browser step that makes hardware acceleration possible.
will-change is a hint that can prepare it; the property choice is what earns it.

terms.definition: Respecting the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting by toning down or removing motion.

en: respect the user's setting to tone motion down
prefers-reduced-motion fallback
turn animations off for people sensitive to motion
zh: 尊重系统的减少动效设置
对晕动敏感的用户关掉或减弱动画

closeTerms.difference: Purposeful animation removes decoration for everyone; reduced motion tones down what remains for users who ask.

antiPatterns.name: Scale from zero
antiPatterns.description: An entrance that starts at scale(0), so the element appears out of nothing instead of from a believable smaller size.
antiPatterns.fix: Start between scale(0.9) and scale(0.97) together with opacity 0; for a popover, also anchor the growth to its trigger.

en: grows from scale 0
starts at scale(0) and zooms up from nothing
pops up out of a single point

antiPatterns.origin: Name listed on aiforui.dev/skills/animation-vocabulary (2026-09-15); not in the public glossary at the locked revision. Description, fix and links are this repository's.

antiPatterns.name: Hover flicker
antiPatterns.description: A hover animation that switches on and off in quick succession: the hovered element moves or scales out from under the pointer, or a touch tap fires a hover that was never meant to run.
antiPatterns.fix: Keep the hit area still (listen on a parent, move the child) and gate hover motion behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).

en: hover state flickers on and off
card jitters when the mouse sits on its edge
hover animation keeps restarting
zh: 鼠标放在边缘时元素来回抖

antiPatterns.origin: Name listed on aiforui.dev/skills/animation-vocabulary (2026-09-15); not in the public glossary at the locked revision. Description, fix and links are this repository's.

antiPatterns.name: Layered entry
antiPatterns.description: Several entrance animations stacked on one arrival: a container and its children each fade, slide or scale on their own clocks, so one appearance reads as competing motions.
antiPatterns.fix: Give the arrival one owner: animate the container once, or stagger the children under a single timeline, not both.

en: too many entrance animations stacked on top of each other
parent and children all animate in at once
everything inside animates in separately while the container animates in
zh: 容器和里面的内容各自都在做入场动画
